August 2024 To, All Members - Unified Payments Interface (UPI) Dear Sir/Madam, Subject: Introduction of “UPI Circle” —- Delegated Payments for secondary users UPI has emerged as a preferred mode of payment for users. UPI has created a seamless digital experience to enable users to transact via their mobile devices. There are users who are still dependent on cash for their daily payment needs because they do not manage their own money through their own account. With the objective of addressing these unmet needs, introduce “UPI Circle” is introduced, wherein UPI users can delegate to their trusted secondary users for making payments. UPI Steering Committee meeting held on 3% August 2023 had endorsed the introduction of “UPI Circle - Delegate Payments”. UPI Circle is a feature where a UPI user acts as a primary to link with their trusted secondary users on their UPI App for either partial or full delegation. Primary user can authorize a trusted secondary user for performing transactions within the security protocols/ limits. Full Delegation — Primary user authorizes a secondary user to initiate and complete UPI transactions as per defined spend limits Partial Delegation — Primary user authorizes initiation of payment requests from secondary users, Primary user shall complete UP! transaction with

claims.text: OC 186A is titled 'Enhancement - UPI Tap & Pay on Point of Sale (PoS)' and was issued on September 10, 2026.
The circular extends UPI Tap & Pay via NFC to Point of Sale (PoS) terminals, allowing users to make contactless payments by tapping their unlocked mobile device on the terminal.
UPI Tap & Pay transactions on PoS terminals are accepted only for Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions.
Payee PSPs must enable UPI Tap & Pay only on NFC-enabled PoS terminals certified in accordance with PCI PTS / CPOC standards.
UPI Application Providers/PSP Banks must obtain explicit user consent after each device binding operation before allowing further transactions.
Remitter Banks must validate the User's account for UPI Tap & Pay feature enablement status before processing each transaction.
Members and UPI Application Providers must obtain explicit user consent for enabling the UPI Tap & Pay feature, with users having the ability to opt out at any time.
Payee PSPs shall integrate the Point-of-Sale Common Library for UPI (PoS CL) at the PoS terminal and complete integration on all terminals under their acquiring network.
UPI Application Providers must ensure device lock is enabled as a prerequisite for activating UPI Tap & Pay, and the device must be unlocked at the time of initiating a transaction.
The per-transaction limit for UPI Tap & Pay is capped at ₹5000, up to which additional factor of authentication shall not be required.
UPI Application Providers must ensure UPI Tap & Pay is made available through a dedicated call-to-action, presented as a standalone feature and not embedded within other services or menus.
Settlement, reconciliation, dispute management, and Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) for UPI Tap & Pay transactions must be carried out in accordance with extant UPI guidelines.
Members shall be guided by RBI guidelines on 'Harmonization of Turn Around Time (TAT) and customer compensation for failed transactions using authorized Payment Systems' dated September 20, 2019.
Members and UPI Application Providers shall refer to the applicable UPI Tap & Pay Feature Document, Technical Specifications, and other instructions issued by NPCI for detailed requirements.

claims.text: OC 186 (2023) introduced UPI Tap & Pay as a new mode for transactions on mobile devices with NFC capability, available on both Android and iOS.
OC 186 required UPI Apps to take permission from the customer to enable NFC for Tap & Pay transactions.
Under OC 186, transaction amounts of Rs. 500 or less could be processed through UPI LITE account if enabled by the user; otherwise, a UPI PIN was required.
Under OC 186, transaction amounts exceeding Rs. 500 required a UPI PIN and were processed online.
OC 186 specified that the initiation mode '06' shall be used for UPI Tap & Pay transactions.
OC 186 required acquiring banks to ensure NFC tags inside UPI Smart QRs/Tags were NFC forum certified (Type 2) and non-rewritable post personalisation.
OC 186 required acquiring banks to procure NFC Tags from NPCI empanelled vendors.
OC 186A (2026) extended UPI Tap & Pay to Point of Sale (PoS) terminals, enabling users to make contactless NFC-based payments by unlocking their mobile device and tapping it on the PoS terminal.
OC 186A requires UPI Tap & Pay transactions on PoS terminals to be accepted only for Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions.
OC 186A requires Payee PSPs to enable UPI Tap & Pay only on NFC-enabled PoS terminals certified in accordance with PCI PTS / CPOC standards.
OC 186A requires explicit User consent after each device binding operation before allowing further transactions using UPI Tap & Pay.
OC 186A requires explicit User consent for enabling the UPI Tap & Pay feature, with users having the ability to opt out at any time.
OC 186A mandates that device lock is enabled as a prerequisite for activating UPI Tap & Pay, and the device must be in an unlocked state at the time of initiating a transaction.
OC 186A caps the per-transaction limit at Rs. 5000, up to which additional factor of authentication is not required.
OC 186A requires Remitter Banks to validate the User's account for UPI Tap & Pay feature enablement status before processing each transaction.
OC 186A allows Users to set their own transaction limits within the aforesaid ceiling of Rs. 5000.

NPCI/UPI/OC-99/2020-21 dated 12" January 2021 on adherence to NPCI guidelines by members / participants and Self-Attestation. Self-Attestation is a process where members / participants declare themselves as compliant with NPCI guidelines. The Self-Attestation checklist is based on documents — Procedural Guidelines, Operating Circulars, Technical Specification Document, etc. Members / participants shall submit Self-Attestation through PCOMP portal confirming Compliance. The Self-Attestation activity shall be on a periodic basis such as annually / quarterly or as and when required. We also refer to the circular no. NPCI/2023-24/PD/005 dated 28" December 2023 on New PCOMP (Product Compliance) portal for Self-Attestation from F.Y. 2023-24 for Members / Participants. The new portal is live and Self-attestation request for Q1 and Q2 of F.Y. 2023-24 along with directives which are to be complied with annually are made available. This is to inform you that directives for Q3 of F.Y. 2023-24 have been updated on the New PCOMP portal for Self-Attestation by members / participants. Members / participants to submit the self- attestation by 31S March 2024. Action for members/participants:

sources.text: fs Conroe =) NPCI/UPI/OC no.199/2024-25 25" June 2024 To, All Members, UPI (Unified Payment Interface) Dear Sir/Madam, Subject: Update to NPCI CL version 1.8 or above UPI has become a preferred digital payment mode across the country. It provides ease of use, convenience and superior user experience with security and interoperability. To ensure the safety and security of the UPI systems, NPCI constantly reviews the security checks of all components in the UPI ecosystem and regularly upgrades them to address evolving threats in cyber landscape. There are security checks implemented as part of the code embedded in the Common Library (CL) along with the feature release to enhance user experience on UPI platforms. Integration of latest versions of CL is important to ensure enhanced security and safety in UPI ecosystem. With this objective, NPCI will be retiring the support for CL prior to Version 1.8 after 30% September 2024. To ensure compliance PSP Banks shall certify and enable CL 1.8 or above and their respective UPI Apps shall integrate the latest version of CL within their application, on or before 30% September 2024. Members are requested to take note of this compliance and communicate it to relevant stakeholders and their respective partners. Yours sincerely, SD/- Kunal Kalawatia Chief of Products 1001A, The Capital, B Wing, 10* Floor, Bandra Kurla Complex,
sources.title: Update to NPCI CL version 1.8 or above
